How this works: Below you'll find a preview of what we plan to ask in each interview, followed by a call for a local videographer who fits our criteria. If you shoot in one of these cities — or know someone who does — we want to hear from you. Every proposal includes the city's top 3 tourist attractions, weather patterns, and airport transfer logistics so you know exactly what we're covering.

East Asia (18 Cities)

From Tokyo's neon rain to Chongqing's fog, East Asia rewards compact, weather-aware kits.

1. Tokyo, Japan Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Tokyo After Dark: A Night-Market Videographer on Shooting Neon in the Rain with a Pocket Gimbal"

What we'll ask: Tokyo's neon-lit alleys and rain-slicked pavements are iconic, but exposing for Shibuya's digital billboards without blowing out highlights takes discipline. We'll ask about pocket-gimbal etiquette in crowded markets like Ameyoko, rain protection that doesn't require a bulky housing, and the exact shutter speed they use to capture motion blur on a moving train. We also want to know where tripods are quietly tolerated — and where they're not.

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Sensō-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest temple, best captured during blue hour when the lanterns glow.
  • Shibuya Scramble Crossing — The world's busiest pedestrian intersection, filmed from the Starbucks second-floor window.
  • Meiji Jingu Shrine — A serene forested shrine that offers contrast to the city's neon chaos.
☀️ Weather Reality

Tokyo's summer (June–August) is hot and humid with frequent rain, while winter (December–February) offers crisp, clear air but shorter daylight hours. The sweet spots are spring (March–May) for cherry blossoms and autumn (October–November) for vibrant foliage.[reference:0][reference:1]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Narita Airport (NRT) is 60 km east — take the Narita Express (N'EX) to Tokyo Station (~60 min, ¥3,070). Haneda Airport (HND) is closer via monorail (~30 min, ¥500).[reference:2]

📢 Call for a Tokyo Videographer

We need: A shooter who films Tokyo weekly — street documentaries, wedding films, or consistent vlogs all qualify. You must have published footage shot in Tokyo within the last 6 months and have lived here for 3+ years.

What you get: Your work linked to your public portfolio, named credit as a verifiable source, and the chance to show the world how Tokyo is really filmed — from the streets, not from a desk.

Apply: Reach out via the footer contact. Include a link to your recent Tokyo footage and your favorite place to film in the city.

2. Shanghai, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"The Bund Blueprint: A Timelapse Artist on Filming Shanghai from Dawn Mist to Neon"

What we'll ask: Shanghai's Bund offers the most iconic urban skyline in Asia — but the light changes from misty dawn to neon night in a matter of hours. We'll ask about day-to-night timelapse ramps, tripod rules on the Bund (where they're technically prohibited), and how to deal with the city's famous haze. We also want to know which metro lines get you to the best elevated viewpoints.[reference:3]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • The Bund — The 1.5 km waterfront with colonial-era buildings facing Pudong's futuristic skyline.[reference:4]
  • Oriental Pearl Tower — The iconic TV tower with observation decks offering panoramic city views.[reference:5]
  • Yu Garden — A classical Ming-dynasty garden in the Old City, perfect for detailed b-roll.[reference:6]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer clear skies and comfortable 15–22°C temperatures. Summer (June–August) is hot and rainy.[reference:7][reference:8]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Pudong International Airport (PVG) connects via Metro Line 2 to the city center.[reference:9] Hongqiao Airport (SHA) is closer for domestic flights.

📢 Call for a Shanghai Videographer

We need: A local shooter who knows the Bund's permit loopholes, the best time-lapse windows, and where to find the city's quieter corners. Must have 3+ years in Shanghai and recent published work.

Apply: Contact us via the footer with your portfolio and a note about your favorite Shanghai filming spot.

3. Beijing, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Hidden Hutongs: A Local Filmmaker on Permits, Drones, and Shooting Where Tourists Can't"

What we'll ask: Beijing's hutongs are disappearing, but they remain the city's soul. We'll ask about drone registration reality (it's stricter than most visitors assume), hutong access etiquette, and filming near protected sites like the Forbidden City. We also want to know which hutong offers the best light at golden hour — and which are best avoided due to permit restrictions.[reference:10]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Forbidden City — The imperial palace complex, requiring tickets booked days in advance.[reference:11]
  • Temple of Heaven — An iconic circular temple set in a vast park, best at sunrise.[reference:12]
  • Summer Palace — A sprawling imperial garden with a lake and pavilions, perfect for wide shots.[reference:13]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–October) offer stable weather and clear skies. Summer is hot and humid; winter is cold with occasional snow.[reference:14][reference:15]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Beijing Capital International Airport (PEK) connects via Airport Express to Dongzhimen, then transfer to the subway system.[reference:16]

📢 Call for a Beijing Videographer

We need: A filmmaker who navigates Beijing's permit system daily and knows which hutongs still feel authentic. Recent published work required.

Apply: Send your portfolio and a brief note about your favorite hutong to film.

4. Osaka, Japan Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Dotonbori One-Handed: A Street-Food Vlogger on Filming While Eating"

What we'll ask: Osaka is Japan's kitchen, and Dotonbori is its busiest food street. We'll ask about one-hand rigs for shooting while eating, close-focus food shots that make takoyaki look cinematic, and night-market audio in crowd noise. We also want to know which lens they use for the iconic Glico Man sign — and how they avoid getting food on their gear.[reference:17][reference:18]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Dotonbori — Osaka's neon-lit entertainment district with giant mechanical signs and endless street food.[reference:19]
  • Osaka Castle — A historic castle surrounded by a park, spectacular during cherry blossom season.[reference:20]
  • Shinsekai — A retro neighborhood with the Tsutenkaku Tower and old-school Osaka atmosphere.[reference:21]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring and autumn offer the most pleasant weather. Summers are hot and humid (June–August, 25–33°C).[reference:22][reference:23]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Kansai International Airport (KIX) is about 35–50 minutes from the city by train express.[reference:24]

📢 Call for an Osaka Videographer

We need: A street-food vlogger or documentary shooter who knows Dotonbori's rhythms. Must have recent Osaka footage.

Apply: Contact us with your portfolio and your go-to Osaka food stall.

5. Chongqing, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"The 8D City: A Drone Pilot on Navigating Chongqing's Vertical Maze in Perpetual Fog"

What we'll ask: Chongqing is China's "mountain city" — a vertical maze where buildings stack on top of each other and the light rail runs through apartment blocks. We'll ask about fog flying (visibility is often poor), multi-level city composition, and battery care in the city's notorious humidity. We also want to know where the drone rules are loosest — and where they're enforced.[reference:25][reference:26]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Hongyadong — A stilt-house complex that looks like it's from Spirited Away, spectacular at night.[reference:27]
  • Yangtze River Cableway — A cable car crossing the river, offering dramatic cityscape views.[reference:28]
  • Ciqikou Ancient Town — A historic riverside town with narrow alleys and traditional architecture.[reference:29]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer comfortable weather. Summer is hot and humid; winter is mild but foggy.[reference:30][reference:31]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Jiangbei International Airport (CKG) has direct subway access to downtown via Line 10 and Line 3.[reference:32][reference:33]

📢 Call for a Chongqing Videographer

We need: A drone pilot or urban explorer who films Chongqing's vertical chaos weekly. Must have recent work.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best fog-flying tip.

6. Guangzhou, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Guangzhou Unboxed: A Commercial Videographer on Filming the World's Factory Floor"

What we'll ask: Guangzhou is the world's factory floor — but it's also a city of colonial heritage and neon-lit night markets. We'll ask about industrial b-roll techniques, mixed-color-temperature lighting in factories and markets, and filming permissions in the city's sprawling wholesale districts. We also want to know which lens they use for the Canton Tower at night.[reference:34]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Canton Tower — The iconic 600-meter tower with sweeping city views, best at sunset or night.[reference:35]
  • Shamian Island — A colonial-era island with European-style architecture and peaceful streets.[reference:36]
  • Yuexiu Park — Home to the Five Rams statue, a symbol of Guangzhou, with lakes and gardens.[reference:37]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring (March–May) and autumn (October–December) are the sweet spots. Summers are hot and humid with frequent rain.[reference:38][reference:39]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Baiyun International Airport (CAN) connects via Metro Line 3 to the city center.[reference:40]

📢 Call for a Guangzhou Videographer

We need: A commercial or documentary shooter who knows the factory districts and market permit rules.

Apply: Contact us with your portfolio and a note about your favorite Guangzhou filming location.

7. Tianjin, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Twin Faces: An Architecture Vlogger on Colonial Facades and Cyberpunk Bridges"

What we'll ask: Tianjin is a city of two faces — colonial-era Western architecture alongside futuristic bridges. We'll ask about wide-angle discipline for capturing the Italian-style buildings, blue-hour bridge shots along the Haihe River, and winter shooting when temperatures drop below freezing. We also want to know which street offers the best colonial facades.[reference:41][reference:42]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Five Avenues — A district of colonial-era mansions with Western architectural styles.[reference:43]
  • Italian Style Street — A pedestrian area with European-style buildings and cafes.[reference:44]
  • Haihe River — The city's river with bridges that light up dramatically at night.[reference:45]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring and autumn offer clear skies and crisp air. Summers are hot and humid; winters are windy and cold.[reference:46][reference:47]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Tianjin Binhai International Airport (TSN) is about 1 hour from the city center by subway or taxi.[reference:48]

📢 Call for a Tianjin Videographer

We need: An architecture or travel vlogger who knows the city's colonial and modern sides.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best blue-hour bridge shot.

8. Shenzhen, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Inside DJI's Hometown: A Tech Reviewer on Testing Drones Where They're Born"

What we'll ask: Shenzhen is the birthplace of DJI, and the city is a testing ground for drone tech. We'll ask about electronics-market filming etiquette, first-look gear testing in the city's tech hubs, and urban drone law — where can you actually fly legally in this hyper-regulated city? We also want to know which park offers the best skyline views.[reference:49]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Window of the World — A theme park with miniature replicas of global landmarks.[reference:50]
  • Ping An Finance Center — One of the world's tallest buildings with observation decks.[reference:51]
  • OCT-LOFT Creative Park — A former factory turned arts district with street art and galleries.[reference:52]
☀️ Weather Reality

Summer (June–August) averages 28–32°C with sea breezes. Spring and autumn are the most comfortable.[reference:53]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport (SZX) connects via Metro Line 11 to downtown.[reference:54]

📢 Call for a Shenzhen Videographer

We need: A tech reviewer or drone pilot who knows the city's drone regulations and best testing spots.

Apply: Contact us with your portfolio and a note about your favorite Shenzhen filming location.

9. Seoul, South Korea Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"The K-Culture Lens: A Fan-Cam Specialist on Concert Etiquette and 4K Zoom"

What we'll ask: Seoul is the epicenter of K-pop and K-culture, and fan-cam specialists have mastered the art of concert filming. We'll ask about concert filming rules (they're stricter than you think), long-zoom compacts that can reach the stage, and palace-to-neon transitions — how to go from shooting Gyeongbokgung Palace at sunset to Hongdae's nightlife in one evening.[reference:55][reference:56]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Gyeongbokgung Palace — The largest of Seoul's five grand palaces, with stunning architecture.[reference:57]
  • Bukchon Hanok Village — A traditional Korean village with narrow alleys and tile-roofed houses.[reference:58]
  • Namsan Tower — A communications tower with panoramic city views and "love locks" fencing.[reference:59]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring (April–May) and autumn (September–October) offer mild weather. Winters are cold and dry with occasional snow.[reference:60][reference:61]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Incheon International Airport (ICN) is about 45 minutes to 1 hour from the city by AREX train or bus.[reference:62]

📢 Call for a Seoul Videographer

We need: A fan-cam specialist, concert shooter, or street vlogger who knows Seoul's nightlife and palace lighting.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best concert footage.

10. Nagoya, Japan Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Precision City: An Industrial Videographer on Filming Bullet Trains at 1/2000s"

What we'll ask: Nagoya is Japan's industrial heart — home to Toyota and bullet trains. We'll ask about high-shutter motion freezing for capturing Shinkansen trains, station filming rules (they're stricter than you'd expect), and industrial access for factory-floor footage. We also want to know which lens they use for Nagoya Castle's golden shachihoko (tiger-fish) ornaments.[reference:63][reference:64]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Nagoya Castle — A historic castle with golden shachihoko ornaments and a reconstructed keep.[reference:65]
  • Atsuta Shrine — One of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, with a sacred sword.[reference:66]
  • Toyota Commemorative Museum — A museum showcasing the history of Toyota and Japanese industry.[reference:67]
☀️ Weather Reality

Spring and autumn offer pleasant temperatures. Summers are hot and humid; winters are cold with occasional snow.[reference:68]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO) connects via Meitetsu train to Nagoya Station (~30 min).

📢 Call for a Nagoya Videographer

We need: An industrial or transport videographer who films trains, factories, or the city's industrial heritage.

Apply: Contact us with your portfolio and your best bullet train shot.

11. Hong Kong Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Vertical Hours: A Trail-and-Tower Vlogger on Victoria Peak to Dai Pai Dong in One Day"

What we'll ask: Hong Kong is a vertical city — from Victoria Peak to street-level dai pai dong stalls. We'll ask about hike-and-shoot kits for trails like Dragon's Back, skyline compression techniques for the iconic harbour view, and street-stall discretion when filming in busy markets. We also want to know which Peak tram carriage offers the best angle.[reference:69][reference:70]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Victoria Peak — The city's highest viewpoint with panoramic harbour and skyline views.[reference:71]
  • Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade — The waterfront with the Avenue of Stars and iconic skyline views.[reference:72]
  • Star Ferry — The classic harbour crossing with unparalleled city views from the water.[reference:73]

Spring (March–May) and autumn (October–December) offer mild, pleasant weather. Summers are hot and humid.[reference:74]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Hong Kong International Airport (HKG) connects via Airport Express to Central Station (~24 min).[reference:75]

📢 Call for a Hong Kong Videographer

We need: A trail-and-tower vlogger who hikes Hong Kong's peaks and films its street-level chaos.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best Peak-to-street transition shot.

12. Dongguan, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Off the Clock: A Factory-Town Filmmaker on Finding Poetry in Production Lines"

What we'll ask: Dongguan is the world's factory — but it also has hidden gardens and ancient villages. We'll ask about documentary access to production lines, fluorescent-light white balance challenges, and minimal kits for discreet filming. We also want to know which factory district offers the most cinematic b-roll — and where to find the city's quiet corners.[reference:76][reference:77]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Songshan Lake — A scenic lake with cycling paths and Huawei's European-style campus.[reference:78]
  • Keyuan Garden — One of the four famous Lingnan gardens, with pavilions and ponds.[reference:79]

October to December offers the most pleasant weather. Summers are hot and humid with typhoon risks.[reference:81][reference:82]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Dongguan has no commercial airport — fly into Guangzhou Baiyun (CAN) or Shenzhen Bao'an (SZX) and take a train or bus.

📢 Call for a Dongguan Videographer

We need: A documentary or industrial filmmaker who knows the city's factory floors and hidden gardens.

Apply: Contact us with your portfolio and a note about your favorite Dongguan filming location.

13. Hangzhou, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

What we'll ask: Hangzhou is China's livestream capital — and West Lake is its most filmed location. We'll ask about livestream setups that work in crowded tourist areas, misty-lake sunrise windows (the best light is before 7 AM), and product-plus-place framing for tea and silk sellers. We also want to know which bridge offers the most iconic West Lake shot.[reference:83][reference:84]

  • Xixi Wetland — A national wetland park with waterways and traditional villages.[reference:87]

Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) are the best seasons. Summer is hot and humid; winter is chilly and damp.[reference:88][reference:89]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport (HGH) connects via Metro Line 19 or airport buses.[reference:90][reference:91]

📢 Call for a Hangzhou Videographer

We need: A livestream creator or travel vlogger who films West Lake's misty mornings and tea plantations.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best West Lake sunrise shot.

14. Foshan, China Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Kung Fu Frames: A Martial-Arts Documentarian on Why 120fps Changed Everything"

What we'll ask: Foshan is the home of Wing Chun and the real-life origin of many kung fu films. We'll ask about slow-motion techniques for capturing fast martial-arts movements, ancestral-hall low-light challenges, and sound design for kung fu performances. We also want to know which temple offers the best lighting for martial-arts documentaries.[reference:92][reference:93]

Spring and autumn are the best seasons. Summer is hot and humid (27–36°C) with frequent rain.[reference:97][reference:98]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Fly into Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport (CAN) and take the airport bus or subway to Foshan (~1–1.5 hours).[reference:99]

📢 Call for a Foshan Videographer

We need: A martial-arts documentarian who knows the city's kung fu heritage and temple etiquette.

Shenyang Taoxian International Airport (SHE) connects via Metro Line 2 to the city center (~40 min).[reference:107]

📢 Call for a Shenyang Videographer

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best winter shot.

Chengdu has two airports — Tianfu (TFU, Metro Line 18) and Shuangliu (CTU, Metro Line 10).[reference:114]

South & Southeast Asia (14 Cities)

Heat, humidity, monsoon, and the most photogenic chaos on Earth.

19. Delhi, India Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"Old Delhi at Golden Hour: A Street Documentarian on Keeping Focus in Beautiful Chaos"

What we'll ask: Old Delhi is beautiful chaos — crowded, colorful, and challenging for autofocus. We'll ask about AF tracking in crowds, dust protection for lenses, and golden-hour timing through the city's famous smog. We also want to know which spice market offers the most cinematic frames — and how to avoid getting your gear stolen.[reference:131][reference:132]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Red Fort — The iconic Mughal fortress with red sandstone walls.[reference:133]
  • Qutub Minar — A 73-meter minaret, the tallest in the world.[reference:134]
  • Chandni Chowk — Old Delhi's chaotic spice market and bazaar.[reference:135]
☀️ Weather Reality

The sweet spot is October to March, with mild and sunny days. Summers are brutally hot; monsoons bring heavy rain.[reference:136]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) is 16 km south — take the Airport Metro Express to New Delhi Station (~20 min).[reference:137]

📢 Call for a Delhi Videographer

We need: A street documentarian who films Old Delhi's chaos and knows the city's permit system.

Apply: Send your portfolio and your best golden-hour shot from Chandni Chowk.

20. Dhaka, Bangladesh Interview Preview Collaboration Call

Latin America (7 Cities)

Altitude, carnival, and some of the best food-light on the planet.

44. São Paulo, Brazil Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"São Paulo from the Rooftops: An Urban Explorer on Safe Filming in a Vertical City"

What we'll ask: São Paulo is a vertical city — and the best views are from its rooftops. We'll ask about rooftop access culture (some buildings are easier than others), street-art b-roll in neighborhoods like Vila Madalena, and urban safety protocols for filming in a city with economic disparities. We also want to know which building offers the best panoramic view of Paulista Avenue.[reference:311][reference:312]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • Paulista Avenue — São Paulo's main thoroughfare with cultural institutions.[reference:313]
  • Ibirapuera Park — The city's largest urban park with Niemeyer-designed buildings.[reference:314]
  • MASP (Museum of Art) — The iconic museum with a glass-and-concrete design.[reference:315]
☀️ Weather Reality

April–May and October–November offer the most pleasant weather. Summers (October–March) are rainy.[reference:316][reference:317]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Guarulhos (GRU) and Congonhas (CGH) airports serve the city.

📢 Call for a São Paulo Videographer

We need: An urban explorer who knows rooftop access and safety protocols for filming.

45. Mexico City, Mexico Interview Preview Collaboration Call

"The Color Code: A Food Vlogger on Making Street Tacos Cinematic in Harsh Midday Sun"

What we'll ask: Mexico City's street food is world-famous — but filming it at midday is a lighting challenge. We'll ask about high-altitude harsh light (the city sits at 2,240 meters), ND strategy for controlling exposure, and market-stall rapport for getting permission to film. We also want to know which taco stall offers the most cinematic steam and sizzle.[reference:318][reference:319]

📍 Top 3 Filming Locations
  • National Museum of Anthropology — One of the world's best museums.[reference:320]
  • Chapultepec Castle — A hilltop castle with city views.[reference:321]
  • Coyoacán — The bohemian neighborhood with the Frida Kahlo Museum.[reference:322]
☀️ Weather Reality

November–April is the dry season with pleasant weather. The city is at 2,240m, so pack layers.[reference:323][reference:324]

✈️ Airport Transfer

Benito Juarez International Airport (MEX) is close to the city center (~25–45 min).[reference:325]

📢 Call for a Mexico City Videographer

We need: A food vlogger who knows how to make street tacos look cinematic in harsh light.

How to Apply or Nominate

If you film professionally in any of these 50 cities — or you know someone who does — we want to hear from you. Our selection criteria are simple:

  • Actively working: You must have published footage shot in the city within the last 6 months.
  • Local for 3+ years: You know the city's seasons, light windows, and filming rules from experience.
  • Verifiable work: We link to your channel or portfolio so readers can judge your footage.

What you get: Your work linked to your public portfolio, named credit as a verifiable source, and the chance to show the world how your city is really filmed — from the streets, not from a desk.

Apply: Reach out through the contact details in the footer. Include a link to your recent work and a brief note about your favorite place to film in your city.
